w1.text: Every week, new A.I. tools appear.

w2.text: Skills, models, scanners, agents. Each one promises better work.

w3.text: We collected a hundred and twenty-five of them.

w4.text: So which ones actually work? Which are safe? And which fit the project in front of you?

g1.text: Our answer is a grade, and only proof can raise it.

g2.text: There are six steps, from E zero to E five.

g3.text: E zero: we have only read about it.

g4.text: E one: it did real work in a project.

g5.text: E two: it was checked against a result we wrote down first.

g6.text: The higher steps need many test cases, a second reviewer, and time in production.

c1.text: Before anything is installed, it is scanned.

c2.text: The scanner reads the files, looking for stolen passwords, hidden instructions, or code pulled from the internet.

c3.text: Each finding comes with a severity and a line number, so a person can check it.

c4.text: In twenty-four of fifty-one scans, at least one part was not safe. Those parts are not installed unless a person reads the report and decides.

c5.text: We tested the scanner too, with traps we planted. It rated two of five as only a caution, so the ledger now blocks any high-risk finding until a person reads it.

p1.text: A grade only moves when a tool is used in a real project.

p2.text: Each use is written down: the task, what broke, what was fixed, and the evidence.

p3.text: F F mpeg measured the first draft of this video and found its sound too quiet. We fixed it, and F F mpeg moved up to E two.

p4.text: A hundred and four tools have no successful use in the ledger yet. They stay on file, as candidates and references.

p5.text: Of the twenty-one that have, eighteen are at E one or higher.

k1.text: Here is one tool, start to finish: the voice you are hearing.

k2.text: It entered the ledger with no proof, at E zero.

k3.text: The scan found no known problems, and its model files matched their published fingerprints.

k4.text: Then it recorded the first narration for this video. That real use proposed E one.

k5.text: A person reviewed the proposal and approved it.

k6.text: To reach E two, it needs a check against a result written down first.

n1.text: When a new project starts, the ledger suggests the tools that fit it, and how each one will be tested there.

n2.text: Every new use adds proof, so the next project starts from what was learned.

n3.text: The ledger also learns as it goes.

n4.text: Every problem is written down with its fix: seventy-seven found, sixty-six fixed. And a failed check can become a new rule, like the stricter scan rule.

r1.text: A hundred and twenty-five tools, eighty-five uses, twenty-one decisions. All on record.

r2.text: This is the Tool Research Ledger.
